apis: POST /api/v1/links: new optional fields expiresAt and ttlSeconds; new 400 invalid-expiry
GET /{code}: 410 link-expired for an expired link; 404 at once after a delete (was: 302 until the cache TTL)
dataFlows: create → LinkService validates the expiry → INSERT with expires_at → after commit the cache gets the entry with its expiry (Redis TTL capped)
redirect → L1 → L2 → DB; every Found entry's expiresAt is compared with the clock → 302 or 410
delete → UPDATE status DELETED → after commit evict L1 and L2 → next redirect reads the row and caches a 404
migrations: V3__link_expiry.sql: ALTER TABLE link ADD COLUMN expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ (nullable, no default, no backfill)
riskNotes: Caching: an expiring link must not outlive its expiry in any level; L1's fixed TTL is longer, so the entry itself must carry the expiry.
Rolling deploy: old instances read Redis values as U:<url>; a new format must not change the value for links without an expiry.
Concurrency: evicting before the delete commits would let a concurrent redirect re-cache the old row; evict after commit.
Cross-instance: other instances' L1 can serve a deleted link for up to the L1 TTL (5 minutes).
